rationale: Every supplied artifact use of claim C-CHAL-006 accurately preserves its scope and limitations. The claim describes AMLAS as a public, six-stage, ML-component safety-assurance methodology that links system safety requirements to data, learning, verification, and deployment evidence. It also states AMLAS's self-imposed limitations: it is for ML components only, should not be used alone, and focuses primarily on offline supervised learning. The claim's scope explicitly notes it is 'University of York AMLAS Version 1.1 research guidance; no claim of regulatory acceptance or end-to-end vehicle/aircraft approval'. All artifact uses consistently reflect these details, explicitly mentioning AMLAS's component-level focus, its need for complementary system/domain assurance, and its status as research guidance rather than a regulatory approval or certification. No instances of omitted qualifications, changed status, or inferences presented as authority evidence were found.
